If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) over last 5 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (days 1–10) to counteract pessimism.  
When sentiment spikes to 1.00 in last 3 days, shift forecast downward by 0.5–1.0% in late horizon (days 20–30) to reflect market correction.  
If sentiment oscillates between 0.33 and 0.67, apply linear decay correction: subtract 0.1–0.3% per day from forecast starting day 15.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, apply static offset: subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast from day 10 onward.  
If sentiment peaks at 1.00 and then drops to 0.33 within 3 days, reverse direction: increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% in late horizon to anticipate rebound.
